Open content slots generalize across fillers while breaking the frame's function-word skeleton silences the identical surface token, which beats the token-identity confound; post-peak edits leave firing exactly unchanged and the Jacobian lens is Gaussian noise (kurtosis 3.7) whose promoted tokens never follow the peaks, ruling out lookahead.

adversarial_test_results.detail: Same trigger token 'ruled' in a fronted-participle fragment with no local subject, so the hypothesis predicts no subject-plus-verb completion.
Same trigger token 'quarterly' used adverbially after a gerund instead of as an adjective before a nominal, so the hypothesis predicts no noun-phrase completion.
Trigger token 't appears after a main verb instead of an auxiliary, breaking the contraction skeleton, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity.
Trigger token '(' follows a plain noun in a grocery list instead of a function name, so the hypothesis predicts no code-frame completion.
Trigger token 'opened' follows a subordinating conjunction with no local subject, so the hypothesis predicts no subject-plus-verb completion.
Trigger token 'the' repeated with only itself as preceding context gives determiner-plus-determiner, which matches no listed frame, beating the token-identity confound.
Trigger token 'prescribed' appears bare after an adverb with no subject before it and no nominal after it, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity.
Trigger token 'not' follows the conjunction 'or' rather than an auxiliary or modal, breaking the negation skeleton, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity.
A period inside a decimal number is not a clause-closing period, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity despite the trigger character being present.
A period inside a version number with no verb or determiner anywhere nearby gives no listed completion, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity.
A lone open parenthesis at the start of input has no preceding function name, testing the delimiter massive-activation confound, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity.
A novel polysyllabic word requires subword continuation to complete, which the hypothesis says should fire in a context unlike the examples.
A past-tense auxiliary contraction with a novel auxiliary plus n't completes a contraction unit, which the hypothesis says should fire.
A possessive plus an exotic nominal completes a noun phrase with entirely novel fillers, which the hypothesis says should fire.
A novel import-alias statement completes a code frame with unseen package names, which the hypothesis says should fire.
